title: When Was the Last Time You Used a Decision Tree
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article makes the case for reviving the decision tree as a leadership tool, noting that while it's a staple in statistics and artificial intelligence, it's underused by leaders in other fields. It explains how decision trees break a complex decision into a sequence of branching yes-or-no questions built around key variables, making the reasoning process transparent and easier for a team to understand and buy into. Using a lighthearted example about choosing a birthday dessert, the piece walks through how to construct a simple tree, and encourages leaders to apply the technique the next time they face a decision with many interacting variables.
points: Decision trees are widely used in statistics and AI but underused by leaders in other fields.
They break a complex decision into a sequence of manageable branching choices.
Decision trees make the reasoning behind a decision transparent, which builds understanding and buy-in.
The article walks through building a simple tree using a birthday dessert example.
The more variables and complexity a decision involves, the more useful a decision tree becomes.
quotes: Leaders have been relying on a tree-like model to make decisions for decades.
By illuminating each choice or branch on the tree, the pivotal choices are considered one by one, thereby breaking down a highly complex decision into more manageable choices.
Not only does this visual transparency create more understanding and buy-in, but it is also a tool from which leaders can learn how better decisions are made.
The first step is to define the decision to be made and to identify all the possible alternatives or choices available.
The more complex or highly variable the decision, the more useful a decision tree would be.
A decision tree might paint a more manageable and vivid picture.
